questions: Is the goal to sort the permutation into strictly increasing order (1,2,...,N) or can it be any sorted order (e.g., decreasing)?
When swapping P_i and P_{i+1}, does the cost i refer to the index before swapping or the index after swapping if multiple swaps affect the same positions?
Are we allowed to perform operations in any order, and does the cost accumulate additively, or are there any discounts/penalties for specific sequences?
Does 'minimum total cost' require considering only sequences that end with P sorted, or must we also ensure intermediate states are valid permutations?
If multiple swaps have the same index i at different times, do they always cost i each time, even if the elements at positions i and i+1 change?
Is the operation allowed only on adjacent indices, or can we choose non-adjacent pairs with a cost based on some other rule?
Should the output be an integer, and are there any constraints on the magnitude of the cost that might affect integer overflow?
Does the cost i refer to the 1-based index as given, or is it 0-based indexing (since many programming languages use 0-based)?
